transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve just stopped caring about things I used to enjoy. My fishing gear’s been sitting untouched in the garage, and going into my woodshop feels like a chore now. Even when my kids ask me to play chess, I’m there, but I’m really just going through the motions.
How long have you been noticing this loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been about a year and seven months now—since my wife’s health problems changed everything at home.

Over these past 19 months, has this low mood and loss of interest been present pretty much every day without a break, or have there been stretches—weeks or more—where you felt back to your normal self?
It’s been pretty constant since then—about a year and seven months now, ever since my wife’s health problems changed things at home.
Over these past several months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah. I’m exhausted when I get into bed, but I’ll lie there thinking through bills and schedules. Or I wake up around three or four and just stare at the ceiling until it’s time to leave for the site.
During this time, have you noticed changes in your ability to concentrate or make decisions, such as at work or on daily tasks?

Yeah, definitely. I used to keep all the schedules and subcontractors straight in my head. Now I’ll read the same email three times and still not absorb it, or lose my train of thought in a meeting. Decisions I used to make in five minutes—I just freeze up over them.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past several months?

Yeah. Most days food just tastes like cardboard. I’ll skip breakfast and then barely pick at dinner, even after being on the site all day. My belt’s had to come in a couple notches, and I wasn’t trying to lose weight.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of not wanting to be alive, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Yeah… on the early drives in, before anyone’s awake, I’ve caught myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t make it there. Sometimes I think about steering off the road, and that scares me because it feels too close.
When you have these thoughts about steering off the road, have you made any specific plans to act on them, or do you feel you could keep yourself safe?
I haven’t made a plan, no. It’s more those thoughts coming up when I’m driving alone early in the morning. But the idea of steering off the road feels too close sometimes, and that scares me.
